key_insight: Functional Lagrange multipliers enable exact multi-source DRO reformulation, while affine restrictions yield scalable upper bounds that are tighter than aggregation-based relaxations.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports robust decisions and model training from fragmented evidence without collapsing distinct sources into a single, more conservative ambiguity set.
method: Represent each evidence source by an ambiguity set and optimize against their intersection.
Couple ambiguity sets through functional Lagrange multipliers, then restrict them to affine decision rules for source-wise decomposition.
Use finite conic reformulations in important special cases or subgradient methods for weakly convex losses.
evidence_signal: In portfolio, newsvendor, and binary classification experiments, the affine approximation remains close to computable exact values, scales better than exact methods, and outperforms aggregation-based benchmarks out-of-sample.
watch_item: Affine bounds are not generally exact; exactness is established for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references.
paper_title: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
